images.title: File:Two Towers - Cape Henlopen - Delaware (55008241793).jpg
images.description: The beach at Cape Henlopen was quiet in that late November way. Wide sand, heavy clouds, and the Atlantic rolling in without much interest in being welcoming. The two WWII fire control towers sat back from the water, solid and unchanged, looking out over the shoreline. I made this looking back toward them, using the rocks and surf to pull the scene together and keep the ocean present in the frame.

images.title: File:Fire Control Towers - Cape Henlopen State Park (52528724378).jpg
images.description: On the coast of the Atlantic Ocean in Delaware stands "Tower 5" and just behind it "Tower 6". These fire control towers stood to help defend Delaware Bay and the Atlantic coastline from enemy ships in World War II. When constructed, this was part of Fort Miles. We took a Thanksgiving Day bike ride from the Henlopen campground around Gordons Pond and then walked the beach along the ocean.
